q1: SELECT name FROM drinker WHERE NOT EXISTS(SELECT f.bar FROM frequents AS f, serves AS s WHERE f.drinker = drinker.name AND f.bar = s.bar AND NOT s.beer IN (SELECT beer FROM likes WHERE drinker = drinker.name))
q2: SELECT DISTINCT frequents.drinker FROM frequents WHERE frequents.bar IN (SELECT serves.bar FROM serves WHERE serves.beer IN (SELECT likes.beer FROM likes WHERE likes.drinker = frequents.drinker) GROUP BY serves.bar HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT serves.beer) = (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT likes.beer) FROM likes WHERE likes.drinker = frequents.drinker))

counterexample: INSERT INTO Drinker (name, address) VALUES ('Drinker1', 'Address1'); INSERT INTO Beer (name, brewer) VALUES ('BeerA', 'BrewerA'), ('BeerB', 'BrewerB'); INSERT INTO Likes (drinker, beer) VALUES ('Drinker1', 'BeerA'), ('Drinker1', 'BeerB'); INSERT INTO Bar (name, address) VALUES ('Bar1', 'Address2'); INSERT INTO Serves (bar, beer, price) VALUES ('Bar1', 'BeerA', 5.00);
explanation: Q1 and Q2 are not equivalent. Q1 checks if a drinker does not serve any beer that the drinker likes in any bar. Q2 checks if a drinker's favorite beers (i.e., the beers the drinker likes the most) are the only beers served in the bars the drinker frequents.
counterexample_dsp: A drinker who likes beer A and B, and the drinker frequents a bar that serves beer A but not beer B.
